summary:
Submitted a combined map update, new obligation and direct check for a second, different responsibility.

Context from the index: the earlier finding is confirmed_in_scope (oblig-config-from-durable-entry, check 96a2fe47…), map v2 is the accepted basis, pending_work is empty, and capacity still has 3 audit units, 5 semantic reviews and 7 experiments.

What the product contains (draft-relative submission.json, with plan_config_readout.json, harness_config_readout.go and the updated map.json):

Map increment (base v2, controller assigns the next version): one added behavior b-config-readout (A7) describing the synchronous caller-visible configuration readout, registered as a consumer of f-config-membership with the attributed A2 consequence that the configuration index is the caller's fence for the membership context. It is an addition/dependency with an explicit preserves statement, so no saved Candidate is challenged; source_ids cite api.go 895-903, future.go 255-270 and api.go 1183-1189.

New obligation oblig-config-readout-index (implementation_semantics): Raft.GetConfiguration must report, through the returned future's Index, the log index at which the node's latest configuration was written. It is grounded on a bound declaration (bind-get-configuration, symbol GetConfiguration, lines 897-903): GetConfiguration constructs configurationsFuture with only the configuration value while configurationsFuture.Index() is documented as the index of the latest configuration in use and feeds Raft.Stats' latest_configuration_index; nextConfiguration treats a nonzero prevIndex as the only configuration a change may be applied to.

The check drives a real single-voter cluster to the leader state with the bootstrap configuration (written at index 1) committed and the leader's own no-op committed, admits one config_index_probe carrying the live latest-configuration index, then reads GetConfiguration().Index() plus the Stats readout on the same node. The property asserts reported_index == probe.live_latest_config_index, so a reported zero against a configuration written at index 1 is a violation; no fault injection is used.

Preflight `validate` returned valid=true with no diagnostics. Acceptance, clean-copy execution and the observed result remain with the controller; local compilation is not possible because only the draft directory is writable.
